subject: OSA residuals using "cdf" vs. other methods with a linear gaussian state-space model

messages.author: 0495130141859df9
messages.subject: OSA residuals using "cdf" vs. other methods with a linear gaussian state-space model
parts:
Dear All, 

I have attached files for a simple linear Gaussian state-space model example with a stationary AR1 process on the latent variable and known observation error variances, which are relatively small.  The code does the AR1 process "by hand" rather than use the namespace density. The OSA residuals produced using the cdf method are very different  from (and much worse than) those using other methods which provide similar residuals. It is most likely an error in my code to use the cdf method.

Also, I suspect there is a typo in the help file for TMB::oneStepPredict in the example code for implementing the cdf method (calling  dnorm and pnorm with sd=0). 

Thanks in advance for any help!
Tim

messages.author: 258b98968d0ad8b9
messages.subject: Re: OSA residuals using "cdf" vs. other methods with a linear gaussian state-space model
parts:
Your code is correct and points out some flaws with the CDF method.

First problem, is that the method failed without giving an error or warning. Only NANs to indicate something went completely wrong. I tracked it down to be an issue with random effect initialization that wasn't stable. This is now fixed in the TMB master branch.

The improved initialization gets the cdf method closer to the other two, but unfortunately it's still too inaccurate. This is a known (yet undocumented) issue with the cdf method, that happens exactly when the measurement error is small.

I expect a corrected CDF method can be developed in the future, but for now one has to be very careful when using it for random effect models.
